mainTopic: The end of פרק משוח מלחמה, on exemptions from war and the types of war, and the start of the עגלה ערופה פרק, on its language, the number of judges, and which cases qualify.
overview: This amud finishes the פרק of משוח מלחמה. The משנה explains that soldiers who flee are stopped because running away is where defeat begins. It then says that the exemptions from battle apply only in a מלחמת רשות, and רבי יהודה uses different names for the wars. The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי and רבי יוסי הגלילי disagree about a rabbinic sin. It also shows that a soldier shaking with visible fear goes home according to everyone. רבי יוחנן and רבא explain how the war labels line up, and רבא says the real dispute is about a preventive war. A new פרק then begins on the עגלה ערופה: its words are said in לשון הקודש, and certain bodies and locations are excluded. Finally, the גמרא examines why the תנאים count three or five judges from 'זקניך ושופטיך'. This discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why fleeing soldiers must be stopped
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that running away is the first step toward defeat, and brings two פסוקים to show it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the start of running away is falling. As it says: 'Israel fled before the Philistines, and there was also a great slaughter among the people.' And later it says: 'The men of Israel fled from before the Philistines and fell slain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reason for its earlier rule that guards stand behind the army to stop anyone who runs. Fleeing leads straight to falling in battle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים put fleeing right next to falling or being killed. This shows that once soldiers start to run, a collapse follows. So stopping runners is not cruelty. It protects the whole army.

keyTerms.meaning: the slain, people killed in battle

phrases.english: because the beginning of fleeing is falling,
as it is said: "Israel has fled before the Philistines,
phrases.notes: שמואל א 4:17

phrases.english: and there was also a great slaughter among the people,"
and further on it says:
"And the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines
phrases.notes: שמואל א 31:1

phrases.english: and fell down slain, etc."

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fleeing must be stopped because fleeing is the beginning of defeat, as shown by two פסוקים in שמואל.

steps.title: Exemptions apply only to optional wars
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits all the exemptions from army service to a מלחמת רשות. In a מלחמת מצוה everyone goes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: When are these rules said? In optional wars. But in מצוה wars everyone goes out, even a groom from his room and a bride from her wedding canopy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets a limit on everything it said before about who goes home from battle. Those exemptions only work in a war that is optional.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to here, the משנה listed people who return home, such as someone who built a house or married a wife. Now it says these exemptions exist only in a מלחמת רשות. In a מלחמת מצוה there are no exemptions at all. Even a חתן and a כלה in the middle of their wedding must go.

keyTerms.meaning: in what case are these words said? (a formula that limits an earlier rule)
an optional war, one the king chooses to fight

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule that the Torah's list of exemptions from war is not absolute. The type of war decides whether they apply.

phrases.english: In what case are these things said?
phrases.notes: "These things" means all the exemptions from war that the משנה listed before.

phrases.english: In optional wars.
But in wars that are a מצוה,
everyone goes out,
even a groom from his room
and a bride from her wedding canopy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of all the exemptions the משנה listed before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exemptions apply only in a מלחמת רשות. In a מלחמת מצוה everyone goes, even a חתן and a כלה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's version: מצוה wars versus obligatory wars
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the exemptions apply in a מלחמת מצוה, and that everyone goes out only in a מלחמת חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When are these rules said? In מצוה wars. But in obligatory wars everyone goes out, even a groom from his room and a bride from her wedding canopy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה repeats the same structure as the first opinion but with different labels. For him, the exemptions work in a 'מצוה' war, and no one is exempt in a 'חובה' war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first opinion the split is רשות versus מצוה. For רבי יהודה it is מצוה versus חובה. So the question becomes which kind of war each label refers to. רבי יוחנן and רבא work this out in steps 12-15.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume רבי יהודה's 'מצוה' means the same thing as the first opinion's 'מצוה'. He uses the words differently. The גמרא later works out how his labels match up with the first opinion.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים —
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: In what case are these things said?
In wars that are a מצוה.
But in obligatory wars,
everyone goes out,
even a groom from his room
and a bride from her wedding canopy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים בְּמִלְחֲמוֹת מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion on how to label the wars in which the exemptions apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the exemptions apply in a מלחמת מצוה. In a מלחמת חובה everyone goes.

steps.title: What is the difference between רבי יוסי and רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what practical difference there is between the two opinions in the משנה about 'the fearful one'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What difference is there between רבי יוסי and רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and goes back to an earlier dispute in the משנה. It asks what the real-life difference is between two opinions that seem very close. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה, both רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי יוסי linked 'the fearful one' to sins. Since both connect fear to sin, the גמרא wants to know where they actually disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is there (as a difference)

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי?
phrases.english: between Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the part of the משנה about the one who is 'fearful and fainthearted' because of his sins.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between the opinions of רבי יוסי and רבי יוסי הגלילי about which sins send a soldier home.

steps.title: The difference is a rabbinic sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that they disagree about someone who broke only a rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a sin that is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The two opinions differ about whether a sin that is only דרבנן is enough to send a soldier home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, any sin, even a rabbinic one, makes a soldier 'fearful' and sends him home. For רבי יוסי, only the kind of תורה-level sin listed in his opinion in the משנה counts.

keyTerms.meaning: there is a difference between them
a sin against a rabbinic law

phrases.english: There is (a difference) between them
regarding a rabbinic sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the practical difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about a rabbinic sin. רבי יוסי הגלילי sends the soldier home for it, and רבי יוסי does not.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי counts even rabbinic sins. רבי יוסי counts only תורה-level sins.

steps.title: Whose view does the ברייתא about talking between תפילין follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: someone who talked between putting on the two תפילין has a sin and goes home from battle. It asks which תנא this follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion does this ברייתא follow? 'One who talked between the hand תפילין and the head תפילין has a sin on his hands, and because of it he goes back from the ranks of war.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא and asks which side of the dispute it fits. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Talking between the two תפילין is a fairly small wrong. Yet the ברייתא says it is enough to send a soldier home. This fits the difference the גמרא just described, about whether minor sins count.

keyTerms.meaning: the ranks of the army arranged for battle

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which was taught:
One who talked between one תפילין and the other
phrases.notes: Here תפילה means one of the תפילין: the one on the arm and the one on the head.

phrases.english: has a sin on his hands,
and he goes back because of it from the ranks of war.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the ברייתא about talking between תפילין follows.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who sends a soldier home even for a minor sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion? רבי יוסי הגלילי's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that the ברייתא matches רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only רבי יוסי הגלילי sends a soldier home for a small sin like this one. So the ברייתא must follow him. It also gives a concrete example of the difference from Step 5.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about which תנא the ברייתא follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, since he counts even minor sins.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about talking between the two תפילין is a clear example of רבי יוסי הגלילי's view that even a minor sin sends a soldier home.

steps.title: Which תנא sends home a soldier shaking with fear?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a soldier who trembles at the sounds of battle, or wets himself in fear, goes home. It suggests this follows רבי עקיבא and not רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught this ברייתא? If a soldier heard horns and trembled, heard shields clashing and trembled, or heard swords being sharpened and urine ran down his knees, he goes home. Shall we say this follows רבי עקיבא and not רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא and asks which opinion it matches. It suggests רבי עקיבא, who reads 'the fearful one' as someone who is simply scared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 tied a sin-based ברייתא to רבי יוסי הגלילי. Now the גמרא tests the other side. This ברייתא is about plain fear, not sin, so it seems to fit only רבי עקיבא. The next step shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי accepts it too.

keyTerms.meaning: the sharpening or polishing of swords
shall we say? (the גמרא offers a guess it may later reject)

phrases.english: Who is the תנא who taught this, which the Rabbis taught:
If he heard the sound of horns and trembled,
or the clashing of shields and trembled,
or the sharpening of swords,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַיִם שׁוֹתְתִין לוֹ עַל בִּרְכָּיו — חוֹזֵר.
phrases.english: and water was trickling down his knees, he goes home.
phrases.notes: 'Water' is a polite way of saying urine.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this? Shall we say it is רבי עקיבא
and not רבי יוסי הגלילי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question pattern as step 6, now applied to a ברייתא about fear instead of sin.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does this ברייתא follow only רבי עקיבא, or could רבי יוסי הגלילי agree with it too?

steps.title: Even רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees in this extreme case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in such an extreme case even רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees the soldier goes home, because the פסוק worries that he will make his brothers afraid.
steps.simpleTranslation: In this case even רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees, because it is written: 'so that he does not melt his brothers' hearts like his own heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the guess from step 8. A soldier this visibly terrified goes home according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי usually reads 'fearful' as afraid because of one's sins. Still, the פסוק itself gives a reason to send someone home: his fear can spread to others. A soldier shaking and wetting himself clearly spreads panic, so even רבי יוסי הגלילי sends him home.

keyTerms.meaning: the hearts of his brothers, his fellow soldiers

steps.whatToRemember: Fear so strong that it shows on the outside sends a soldier home according to everyone, because it would scare the whole army.

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי מוֹדֶה,
phrases.english: In this case even רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees,
because it is written:
"so that he does not melt the heart of his brothers like his own heart."
phrases.notes: דברים 20:8

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by showing the ברייתא fits both opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both opinions agree, because the פסוק's concern about fear spreading to others applies to anyone this visibly terrified.

steps.title: The משנה's words about running away seem backwards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the officers and points out that the phrase 'the beginning of fleeing is falling' seems reversed. It should say 'the beginning of falling is fleeing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And when the officers finish...' This line, 'because the beginning of fleeing is falling,' should instead say 'because the beginning of falling is fleeing'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and challenges its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה explains why guards may strike soldiers who run away. The logic is that running away leads to defeat. So the wording should be 'defeat starts with running away,' not the other way around.

phrases.english: "And it will be, when the officers finish," etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה, which quotes דברים 20:9.

phrases.english: This line, "because the beginning of fleeing is falling":

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁתְּחִילַּת נְפִילָה נִיסָה מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: it should have said "because the beginning of falling is fleeing"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a later line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה: 'the beginning of fleeing is falling.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fleeing causes defeat, not the other way around, so the order of the words seems backwards.

steps.title: Read it the other way around
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees and tells us to read the משנה as 'the beginning of falling is fleeing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: 'because the beginning of falling is fleeing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and corrects how the line should be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no clever defense here. The גמרא simply says to read the line in the logical order: defeat begins when soldiers start running away.

phrases.english: Say: "because the beginning of falling is fleeing."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the wording challenge from step 10 and fixes the reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means that defeat begins with running away.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the two sides just use different names
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's line about optional wars, רבי יוחנן explains that what the חכמים call רשות, רבי יהודה calls מצוה, and what the חכמים call מצוה, רבי יהודה calls חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'When does this apply? In optional wars...' רבי יוחנן said: the 'optional' war of the חכמים is the 'מצוה' war of רבי יהודה, and the 'מצוה' war of the חכמים is the 'חובה' war of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, and רבי יוחנן explains how the two opinions' war names line up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the חכמים use the names רשות and מצוה, and רבי יהודה uses מצוה and חובה. רבי יוחנן says they are describing the same two kinds of war with different labels. So the exemptions from battle apply to the same kind of war on both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: an optional war, one the king may choose to fight
a war that is a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: The same word means different wars depending on who is talking. When the חכמים say מצוה, they mean what רבי יהודה calls חובה. When רבי יהודה says מצוה, he means what the חכמים call רשות.

phrases.aramaic: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים בְּמִלְחֲמוֹת הָרְשׁוּת כּוּ׳,
phrases.english: "When do these words apply? In optional wars," etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. 'These words' are the exemptions that send soldiers home.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
The "optional" war of the Rabbis
is the "מצוה" war of רבי יהודה,
and the "מצוה" war of the Rabbis
is the "obligatory" war of רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רְשׁוּת דְּרַבָּנַן זוֹ הִיא מִצְוָה דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the משנה's last section and the war categories from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים' רשות equals רבי יהודה's מצוה, and the חכמים' מצוה equals רבי יהודה's חובה.

steps.title: רבא: the wars everyone agrees about
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone agrees that יהושע's wars to conquer the land were חובה, and that the wars of בית דוד to expand the borders were רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the wars of יהושע to conquer the land are obligatory according to everyone. The wars of בית דוד to expand the borders are optional according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא first sets out the cases that both sides agree on. This prepares the next step, where he shows where they actually disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא names a clear case at each end. Conquering ארץ ישראל in יהושע's time is a required war. Expanding territory in דוד's time is a choice. Neither of these is the subject of the disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: for expansion, to widen the borders

phrases.english: רבא said:
The wars of יהושע to conquer the land
are obligatory, according to everyone.
The wars of the House of דוד for expansion
are optional, according to everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִלְחֲמוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְכַבֵּשׁ דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל חוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Unlike רבי יוחנן, רבא is heading toward a real disagreement. He starts by naming the cases everyone agrees on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע's wars of conquest are חובה, and בית דוד's wars of expansion are רשות, according to everyone.

steps.title: Where they argue: wars to weaken enemies before they attack
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement is about a war fought to weaken nearby nations so they will not attack. One side calls it a מצוה, and the other calls it רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do they disagree? About a war to weaken the nations so they will not come against Israel. One Sage calls it a מצוה, and the other calls it optional.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא identifies the one type of war the two sides argue about: a war to prevent a future attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A preventive war falls between the clear cases. רבי יהודה calls it a מצוה. The חכמים call it רשות, so for them it is just an optional war.

phrases.english: Where they disagree
is a war to weaken the nations so they will not come against them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the Jewish people.

phrases.english: One Sage calls it a מצוה
and the other Sage calls it optional.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי לְמַעוֹטֵי נׇכְרִים דְּלָא לַיְתֵי עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After naming the agreed cases in step 13, רבא points to the disputed middle case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A preventive war is a מצוה according to רבי יהודה and רשות according to the חכמים.

steps.title: Why it matters: being busy with a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The practical difference is the rule that someone busy with one מצוה is free from doing another. According to the side that calls a preventive war a מצוה, its soldiers are free from other מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical difference is the rule that someone busy with a מצוה is exempt from another מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא ends by showing what changes in practice because of the disagreement over a preventive war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is not just about names. If the war counts as a מצוה, a soldier fighting it is free from other מצוות while he fights. If it is only רשות, he has no such exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: someone busy with one מצוה is free from doing another

steps.whatToRemember: A war fought to stop enemies before they attack is a מצוה for רבי יהודה and רשות for the חכמים. The difference matters for whether its soldiers are free from other מצוות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the names of the war categories have real legal results for the soldiers who fight in them.

phrases.english: The practical difference is
regarding one who is busy with a מצוה, who is exempt from another מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ לְעוֹסֵק בְּמִצְוָה שֶׁפָּטוּר מִן הַמִּצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical result of the disagreement described in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: If a preventive war is a מצוה, as רבי יהודה holds, its soldiers are free from other מצוות. If it is רשות, as the חכמים hold, they are not.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the פרק of משוח מלחמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally closes the פרק about the כהן anointed for war.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק משוח מלחמה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the standard closing line marking the end of the פרק about the משוח מלחמה. Nothing new is taught here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרק just ended with the discussion of רשות and מצוה wars and their practical difference. The הדרן line closes that topic so a new פרק can begin.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The closing formula at the end of a פרק
The כהן anointed to speak to the army before war. This is also the name of the פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, Meshuach Milchamah

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק whose last discussion was the practical difference between מצוה and רשות wars.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק of משוח מלחמה is complete.

steps.title: The words of the heifer ceremony are said in Hebrew
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens by stating that the words said at the עגלה ערופה ceremony are said in לשון הקודש, and it quotes the פסוקים that begin this topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: The heifer whose neck is broken: its words are said in the holy language, as it says: 'If a slain person is found in the land... then your elders and your judges shall go out.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins. The משנה says that the declaration made at the עגלה ערופה ceremony must be said in לשון הקודש, and it quotes the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues a list from earlier in מסכת סוטה of things that must be said in לשון הקודש, not in any language. The עגלה ערופה is brought when a murdered person is found and the killer is unknown.

keyTerms.meaning: A young cow whose neck is broken. This ceremony is done when the killer of a murdered person is unknown
Your elders and your judges, the ones who go out to the body

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק quoted here does not mention language at all. That looks strange, and the גמרא will soon ask what the משנה means by quoting it.

phrases.english: The heifer whose neck is broken — in the holy language,
phrases.notes: He means the words the judges say at this ceremony must be said in Hebrew.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'If a slain person is found in the land...'
phrases.notes: דברים 21:1

phrases.english: then your elders and your judges shall go out.'
phrases.notes: דברים 21:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק and a new topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words said at the עגלה ערופה ceremony must be said in לשון הקודש.

steps.title: Three judges from the High Court go out
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that three members of the בית דין הגדול in ירושלים go out to the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three from the Great Court in Jerusalem would go out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now starts explaining the procedure. According to the first opinion, three judges from the בית דין הגדול go out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק said 'your elders and your judges shall go out.' The תנא קמא understands this to mean three judges, and they come from the highest court in ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Great Court, the סנהדרין of 71 judges in ירושלים
Go out, here meaning they leave to examine the body

phrases.english: Three from the Great Court
that is in Jerusalem would go out,

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה מִבֵּית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם הָיוּ יוֹצְאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains who the 'elders and judges' in the פסוק are and how many go out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three members of the בית דין הגדול go out to the body.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says five judges go out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה argues that five go out: two for 'elders,' two for 'judges,' and one more so the court is not an even number.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: five. 'Your elders' means two, 'and your judges' means two, and a court may not be even, so they add one more.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the תנא קמא and says five judges go out. He shows how he reads the numbers from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plural word means at least two, so 'elders' gives two and 'judges' gives another two, which makes four. A court cannot have an even number, so a fifth judge is added.

keyTerms.meaning: A court with an even number of judges, which could end in a tie

steps.confusionAlert: The fifth judge is not taken from the פסוק. He is added only because a court cannot be an even number.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Five,
as it is stated: 'your elders' — two,
phrases.notes: 'Elders' is plural, and the smallest plural is two.

phrases.english: 'and your judges' — two,
and a court may not be evenly numbered,
so they add one more to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the number three given by the תנא קמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, five judges go out: four from the plural words and one added to avoid an even court.

steps.title: Bodies that were hidden, hanging, or floating are excluded
steps.stepSummary: If the body was hidden under stones, hanging on a tree, or floating on water, there is no עגלה ערופה, and each case is learned from a word in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was found hidden in a pile of stones, hanging on a tree, or floating on the water, they did not break the heifer's neck. As it says: 'in the land,' and not hidden in a pile; 'lying,' and not hanging on a tree; 'in the field,' and not floating on the water.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three ways a body can be found where the ceremony is not done. It ties each one to a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the body as 'in the land,' 'lying,' and 'in the field.' Each word excludes one case: a body buried under stones is not 'in the land,' a hanging body is not 'lying,' and a floating body is not 'in the field.'

keyTerms.meaning: They break the neck of the heifer, meaning they do the ceremony

phrases.english: If he was found hidden in a pile of stones
or hanging on a tree
or floating on the surface of the water —
they would not break the heifer's neck,
as it is stated: 'in the land' — and not hidden in a pile,
phrases.notes: דברים 21:1

phrases.english: 'lying' — and not hanging on a tree,
'in the field' — and not floating on the surface of the water.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא טָמוּן בַּגַּל אוֹ תָּלוּי בָּאִילָן אוֹ צָף עַל פְּנֵי הַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who goes out to which bodies qualify for the ceremony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A body that was hidden, hanging, or floating does not get an עגלה ערופה, based on the words of the פסוק.

steps.title: Bodies found near a border, a non-Jewish city, or a city with no court
steps.stepSummary: If the body is closest to the border, to a city that is mostly non-Jewish, or to a city with no בית דין, there is no עגלה ערופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was found near the border, or near a city that is mostly non-Jewish, or near a city with no court, they did not break the heifer's neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives three more cases with no ceremony. This time it depends on where the body was found, not on how it was lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ceremony is done by the closest city. If the closest place is the border, a mostly non-Jewish city, or a city without a בית דין, then no city can bring the heifer.

phrases.english: If he was found close to the border
or to a city whose majority are non-Jews

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְעִיר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ בֵּית דִּין —
phrases.english: or to a city that has no court —
phrases.notes: This means a court of twenty-three judges.

phrases.english: they would not break the heifer's neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more exclusions, based on location instead of the body's position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A body found closest to the border, a mostly non-Jewish city, or a city without a בית דין does not get an עגלה ערופה.

steps.title: We only measure to a city that has a court
steps.stepSummary: When finding the closest city, the judges only measure to cities that have a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only measure to a city that has a court.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a general rule for measuring. Only a city with a בית דין counts as the 'closest city.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judges measure from the body to find the nearest city, and that city brings the heifer. A city without a בית דין is not counted in this measuring at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They measure the distance from the body to the nearby cities

steps.whatToRemember: An עגלה ערופה needs the right kind of body (lying on the ground in the field) and the right kind of nearest city (Jewish majority, inside the land, with a בית דין). The judges who go out are three, or five according to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: They measure only
to a city that has a court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹדְדִין אֶלָּא לְעִיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the 'no court' case from the previous step into a general rule for measuring.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Measuring for the עגלה ערופה is done only to a city with a בית דין.

steps.title: What Is the משנה Trying to Say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by its proof that the עגלה ערופה declaration is said in לשון הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the משנה saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking what the משנה meant. This sets up רבי אבהו's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the עגלה ערופה declaration must be said in לשון הקודש. As its source, it quoted the opening פסוק about finding a body, but that פסוק says nothing about language. So the גמרא asks how this proof is supposed to work.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
What is it saying? (asking for the meaning of an unclear text)

phrases.english: גמרא: What is it saying?
phrases.notes: The question is about the משנה's proof that the עגלה ערופה declaration is said in Hebrew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא now turns back to the משנה's opening claim about the language of the declaration.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does the משנה's quoted פסוק prove that the declaration is in לשון הקודש?

steps.title: Learning the Language From the Word 'They Shall Answer'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that the word 'וענו' links the עגלה ערופה declaration to the לויים's declaration, which was in לשון הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: This is what the משנה means. The פסוק here says 'They shall answer and say.' Elsewhere the תורה says 'The לויים shall answer and say.' Just as the answering there was in לשון הקודש, so too here it is in לשון הקודש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו explains the משנה's proof. The same word 'וענו' appears in both places, so the rule about language is carried over from one to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is not the opening פסוק itself but a later פסוק in the same section, 'וענו ואמרו.' At הר גריזים and הר עיבל, the לויים clearly spoke in לשון הקודש. Because both sections use the word 'וענו,' the same requirement applies to the elders of the עגלה ערופה.

keyTerms.meaning: And they shall answer (the linking word)

phrases.english: רבי אבהו said: This is what it means:
As it says: 'And they shall answer and say,'
phrases.notes: דברים 21:7

phrases.english: And elsewhere it says
'And the לויים shall answer and say, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים 27:14, the blessings and curses at הר גריזים and הר עיבל.

phrases.english: Just as the answering mentioned there
is in the holy language —
so too here it is in the holy language.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The proof comes from the word 'וענו,' which links this declaration to the לויים's declaration in לשון הקודש.
steps.whatToRemember: The עגלה ערופה declaration must be in לשון הקודש because the word 'וענו' connects it to the לויים's declaration.

steps.title: The משנה lays out the procedure: who goes out
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues with the procedure of the עגלה ערופה and repeats that three judges go out, while רבי יהודה says five.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is the procedure of the עגלה ערופה done? 'If a slain person is found in the land... your elders and your judges shall go out.' Three from the בית דין הגדול in ירושלים would go out. רבי יהודה says: five, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: After רבי אבהו's explanation, the משנה itself continues and lays out the order of the עגלה ערופה ceremony. It repeats the dispute about three or five judges from steps 18-19, and the ברייתא in the next steps explains where each number comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is ruled here. The משנה restates the number of judges as the first stage of the procedure. The ברייתא in the next steps gives the reasoning from the פסוק for three and for five.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown
The Great Court, the סנהדרין of 71 in ירושלים
And so on (the rest of the quote is assumed)

phrases.english: And how is the procedure of the עגלה ערופה done?
'If a slain person is found in the land...'
phrases.notes: דברים 21:1-2

phrases.english: 'then your elders and your judges shall go out' —
three from the Great Court
that is in Jerusalem would go out.
Rabbi Yehuda says: five, and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the language question back to the משנה's dispute about the number of judges.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three judges of the בית דין הגדול go out; רבי יהודה says five.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's Count: Five Judges
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה counting two for 'elders,' two for 'judges,' and adding one so the court is not even.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Your elders and your judges shall go out.' 'Your elders' means two, and 'your judges' means two. A court may not be an even number, so we add one more. That makes five. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out how רבי יהודה reaches five judges from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plural word means at least two. רבי יהודה counts both plurals, 'זקניך' and 'שופטיך,' to reach four. Since a court cannot have an even number, one more is added, giving five.

keyTerms.meaning: A court with an even number of judges

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'Then your elders and your judges shall go out.'
'Your elders' means two,
'and your judges' means two,
and a court may not be even,
phrases.notes: שקול literally means 'balanced.' An even court could end in a tie.

phrases.english: so we add one more to them,
so here there are five.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יהודה's number from the משנה quoted in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five judges: two plus two, plus one so the court is not even.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's Count: Three Judges
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון counts only 'elders' as two and adds one, reaching three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'Your elders' means two. A court may not be even, so we add one more. That makes three.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון, who reaches three judges. This matches the תנא קמא of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון counts only the word 'זקניך' as two judges. He does not count 'ושופטיך' at all. Adding one so the court is not even gives three.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
'Your elders' means two,
and a court may not be even,
so we add one more to them,
so here there are three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing count to רבי יהודה's in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three judges: two from 'elders,' plus one so the court is not even.

steps.title: But the פסוק Also Says 'Your Judges'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון: the פסוק also says 'ושופטיך,' so why not count two more?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רבי שמעון too, it is written 'and your judges'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון for ignoring the word 'ושופטיך' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's count seems to skip a whole plural word. If 'זקניך' means two, then 'ושופטיך' should also mean two. That would bring him to five, like רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! (pointing to a פסוק that seems to contradict)

phrases.english: And for Rabbi Shimon too,
isn't it written 'and your judges'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי שמעון's derivation from step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's count of three judges
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'ושופטיך' is also plural and should add two more judges.

steps.title: 'Your Judges' Teaches They Must Be the Distinguished Ones
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון uses 'ושופטיך' to teach that the judges must be the special, top judges, not to add to the number.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that word for 'the distinguished ones among your judges.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון does read 'ושופטיך,' but he uses it for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, 'ושופטיך' teaches who must go: the most distinguished judges, from the בית דין הגדול. Since the word is used for that lesson, it cannot also add to the number.

phrases.english: He needs that word
for the distinguished ones among your judges.
phrases.notes: He means the judges of the בית דין הגדול, as the משנה said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is needed for a different lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ושופטיך' adds two more judges to the count.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ושופטיך' teaches that the judges must be the distinguished ones.

steps.title: Where רבי יהודה Learns 'Distinguished Ones'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns the 'distinguished ones' lesson from the extra letter in 'זקניך' instead of 'זקני.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? He learns it from the fact that the פסוק says 'your elders' and not just 'the elders.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא hints at a question: רבי יהודה uses 'ושופטיך' for the count, so where does he learn that the judges must be distinguished? It answers that he learns it from the extra ending on 'זקניך.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have written just 'זקני' (elders). Instead it wrote 'זקניך' (your elders). רבי יהודה reads that extra ending as teaching 'the distinguished ones,' so 'ושופטיך' stays free to add two judges.

keyTerms.meaning: Elders (the shorter form the פסוק could have used)
It comes out, it is learned from

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים agree the judges must be distinguished. They only disagree about which word in the פסוק teaches it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: The question is left unsaid: where does he learn that the judges must be the distinguished ones?

phrases.english: He learns it from 'elders' becoming 'your elders.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the same issue around to רבי יהודה after רבי שמעון's answer in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds another source in the פסוק for the same lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה has no source for requiring distinguished judges, since he uses 'ושופטיך' for the count.
steps.terutzMaskana: He learns it from the extra ending of 'זקניך.'
steps.whatToRemember: So far: רבי שמעון uses 'ושופטיך' to require distinguished judges and counts three. רבי יהודה gets the 'distinguished' rule from the extra ending of 'זקניך' and counts five. Steps 31-34 refine how each one reads the words.

steps.title: Why רבי שמעון needs both 'your elders' and 'your judges'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains that 'זקניך' rules out ordinary old men, and 'ושופטיך' rules out a small סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון? If the תורה had written only 'elders of,' I would have thought even plain old men from the market count, so it wrote 'your elders.' And if it had written only 'your elders,' I would have thought even a small סנהדרין counts, so it wrote 'and your judges,' meaning the most distinguished of your judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי שמעון uses each word. He reads the extra letter in 'זקניך' as ruling out ordinary old men, and 'ושופטיך' as ruling out a small סנהדרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, 'זקניך' (with 'your') shows these must be real judges, not just old men. 'ושופטיך' narrows it further to the top court, so a small סנהדרין is not enough. Both words teach who the judges are, not how many there are.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
elders of the marketplace: plain old men, not judges
a small סנהדרין, a court of 23

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon: if the Torah had written 'elders of'
I would have said even elders of the marketplace,
phrases.notes: Just ordinary old men, not trained judges.

phrases.english: so the Torah wrote 'your elders.'
And if the Torah had written only 'your elders,'
I would have said even a small Sanhedrin,
so the Torah wrote 'and your judges'
to teach the distinguished among your judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״זִקְנֵי״ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 30 showed רבי יהודה's use of the extra letter, this step shows how רבי שמעון uses both words instead.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word gets its own job (a narrowing step-by-step reading)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One word alone would let in ordinary old men, or a small סנהדרין.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זקניך' requires real judges and 'ושופטיך' requires the top court, so both words are needed and neither adds to the number.

steps.title: רבי יהודה rules out a small Sanhedrin from 'elders of the congregation'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from a גזירה שוה with 'זקני העדה' that the judges must be the top ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה learns 'elders' 'elders' from 'the elders of the congregation': just as there it means the distinguished of the congregation, so too here it means the distinguished of the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה knows a small סנהדרין is not enough, since he uses 'ושופטיך' for the count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'זקני' shows up both here and by the פר העלם דבר of the community, where it means the great סנהדרין. Through a גזירה שוה, רבי יהודה carries that meaning over to our case. So he gets the 'top judges' rule without using 'ושופטיך'.

keyTerms.meaning: learning one place from another through a shared word
the elders of the congregation: the great סנהדרין
just as there… so too here

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda derives
'elders' 'elders' from 'the elders of the congregation':
phrases.notes: ויקרא ד:טו

phrases.english: just as there, it means the distinguished of the congregation,
so too here, the distinguished of the congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי שמעון used 'ושופטיך' to rule out a small סנהדרין, this gives רבי יהודה's separate source for the same rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה uses 'ושופטיך' for counting, he seems to have no source excluding a small סנהדרין.
steps.terutzMaskana: He learns it from 'זקני העדה' through a גזירה שוה.

steps.title: If he uses the shared-word link, why not learn everything from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks: if רבי יהודה uses the גזירה שוה, he could learn the whole law from it, so why are 'זקניך ושופטיך' needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he learns from there, let him learn the whole matter from there. Why do I need 'your elders and your judges'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given for רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה usually carries over everything from one place to the other. If רבי יהודה learns 'top judges' from 'זקני העדה,' the whole law should come from there, and the words 'זקניך ושופטיך' would have no job left. That cannot be, since every word must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need it? (this word seems to have no job)

phrases.aramaic: אִי גָּמַר, לִגְמְרַהּ לְכוּלַּהּ מִילְּתָא מֵהָתָם,
phrases.english: If he derives it, let him derive the whole matter from there;
phrases.notes: Including the number of judges, not only which judges.

phrases.english: why do I need 'your elders and your judges'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי גָּמַר, לִגְמְרַהּ לְכוּלַּהּ מִילְּתָא מֵהָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the גזירה שוה offered in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה learns 'top judges' from 'זקני העדה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גזירה שוה should carry over the whole law, which would leave 'זקניך ושופטיך' with no job.

steps.title: The letter ו׳ in 'and your judges' adds to the count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the גזירה שוה: for רבי יהודה, the ו׳ of 'ושופטיך' is what adds to the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ו׳ of 'and your judges' is for the count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs away from its last answer ('אלא') and gives a new reading of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי יהודה does not use the גזירה שוה. 'ושופטיך' itself teaches that they must be the top judges, and the extra letter ו׳ ('and') is what adds more judges to the count. This way every part of the פסוק has its own job.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't keep the גזירה שוה from step 32. The word 'אלא' means the גמרא has dropped it, and the count now comes from the ו׳ alone.

phrases.english: Rather, the vav of 'and your judges' is for the count.
phrases.notes: So 'ושופטיך' teaches that they're top judges, and the extra 'and' adds more judges to the count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the גזירה שוה answer that step 33 knocked down.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה learns 'top judges' from the גזירה שוה with 'זקני העדה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: He learns 'top judges' from 'ושופטיך', and the ו׳ adds to the count.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the real point of disagreement: does a single letter ו׳ add to the count? That is what the גמרא asks רבי שמעון next.

steps.title: Turning to רבי שמעון's side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask how רבי שמעון reads the ו׳; the answer comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to explain why רבי שמעון does not count the ו׳, and the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה now adds to the count from the ו׳, the גמרא needs to show why רבי שמעון does not. Only the opening words of that move appear here.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and your judges', the word whose ו׳ is in question

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the question of the ו׳ against רבי שמעון, after it became רבי יהודה's source for the count.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does רבי שמעון treat the ו׳ of 'ושופטיך', which רבי יהודה uses to add to the count?
